requirement:
After applying a round's additions, Habeas MUST check freshness against the
edited sources. It MUST reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied
when the writes changed its assessment inputs. It MUST also reassess any other
subject whose previously current evidence those writes made stale, including
definitions, citation reviews, and site reviews outside the initial selection.
Independent reassessments MUST run under {cite}`requirements.authoring.concurrency`.
Each reassessment MUST use fresh inputs and the selected assessment policy.
Only a fresh successful assessment establishes `true`.

A subject with a remaining manual instruction or an action that could not be applied MUST pause for
the rest of the invocation, even if another edit changes its inputs. Other
subjects MUST continue. An already-present marker or stale selector alone MUST
cause no reassessment. If every requested marker already exists and the inputs
are unchanged, the negative judgment stands. Repeat while eligible subjects
remain, with no limit on rounds or automated additions. With `--stdout`, Habeas
MUST report the named subject's assessment and proposed corrections without
editing sources or starting a correction-driven reassessment.
rationale: Add a test, or extend `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[a_named_reference_edit_refreshes_a_definition_and_a_citation_that_read_the_same_text]` or `reference_edits_reassess_a_skipped_subject_sharing_the_changed_input`, so it checks that a reassessment round runs under the configured concurrency. The fixture server already records `Requests.peak`, the timeline and `first_pair_overlapped`. After the reassessment round, assert that `peak` does not exceed the configured value (2), and that two independent reassessments overlap in flight. Use a fixture where at least three independent peers are stale, or configure a lower limit. — `requirements.authoring.reassessment` says "Independent reassessments MUST run under `requirements.authoring.concurrency`". That requirement says in-flight assessments MUST NOT exceed the selected concurrency and that batch work uses asynchronous tasks. No reviewed test covers this for the reassessment round. The reassessment tests set `concurrency = 2` and check which subjects were reassessed. They only check membership in `seen[4..]`, which is order-agnostic, and they never assert `peak` or overlap. A reassessment round that ran its peers strictly serially would pass. So would one that ran them unbounded, for example three peers in flight against a limit of 2. The tests that do assert `peak` and overlap, such as `batch_fills_evidence_preserves_current_records_and_reauthors_only_changed_inputs`, cover the initial batch only. The other obligations are adequately tested. Reassessing subjects with stale evidence is covered by `reference_edits_reassess_a_skipped_subject_sharing_the_changed_input` for a site review and a requirement, and by `a_named_reference_edit_refreshes_a_definition_and_a_citation_that_read_the_same_text` for a citation review. Reassessing a subject whose corrections were all satisfied, repeated rounds, and the selected policy are covered by `corrections_replay_reference_only_mixed_and_regression_findings`, in its reference-only, confirm-reassessment and implementation cases. Pausing is covered by the mixed and new-regression cases and by `a_changed_shared_input_does_not_resume_a_paused_subject`, which also shows other subjects continuing. Already-present and stale markers causing no reassessment is covered by `stale_and_already_present_references_do_not_retry_unchanged_inputs`. `--stdout` is covered by the stdout case.

edited sources. It MUST reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied
when the writes changed its assessment inputs. It MUST also reassess any other
subject whose previously current evidence those writes made stale, including
definitions, citation reviews, and site reviews outside the initial selection.

Each reassessment MUST use fresh inputs and the selected assessment policy.

A subject with a remaining manual instruction or an action that could not be applied MUST pause for
the rest of the invocation, even if another edit changes its inputs. Other
subjects MUST continue. An already-present marker or stale selector alone MUST
cause no reassessment. If every requested marker already exists and the inputs
are unchanged, the negative judgment stands. Repeat while eligible subjects
remain, with no limit on rounds or automated additions. With `--stdout`, Habeas
MUST report the named subject's assessment and proposed corrections without

:::{req} concurrency
Each named authoring configuration MUST accept an optional positive integer
`concurrency` in its configuration table. When omitted, the maximum number of
simultaneous assessments MUST default to the number of available logical CPUs
for Bedrock and OpenAI, falling back to one when that count is unavailable, and to one for
Ollama. A configured value MUST override the default for each backend; zero
MUST be rejected as invalid configuration.
Batch authoring MUST use asynchronous tasks on a runtime with a fixed worker
thread pool. The number of assessments running at once MUST NOT exceed the
selected concurrency. Each assessment MUST retain its own model conversation and
usage record. Transient provider failures, including throttling, MUST be
retried within the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff`; every other provider error MUST
be reported through the ordinary assessment-failure path.
